newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-NORTH AFRICAN CLUBS MARCH THROUGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORTH AFRICAN CLUBS MARCH THROUGH.

text.p: North African clubs, traditionally dominant in all three African club competitions, continued their march through the early stages with no casualties after the weekend's first round, second leg matches.

African Champions' Cup holders Zamalek of Egypt drew 1-1 in Addis Ababa with St George of Ethiopia to go through 3-1 on aggregate and will be joined in the second round by former winners Raja Casablanca of Morocco and Tunisia's Club Africain.

In the Cup Winners' Cup, Cairo's Arab Contractors won 2-0 against Kenyan newcomers Mumais Sugar to progress by the same aggregate score while Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup holders Kawkab Marrakesh were also victorious.
Zamalek, who won the Champions' Cup for a record fourth time last December, took a precarious 2-0 lead away for the second leg on Sunday and had their lead cut in half after 30 minutes.
But Algerian international Kamel Kaci Said took just three minutes to equalise in front of a capacity crowd and allow Zamalek breathing space for the rest of a tight match.
Club Africain were also facing early elimination in their match against Djoliba of Mali in Bamako on Sunday, leading 3-2 from the first leg.
Djoliba quickly evened the aggregate scoreline with Soumailia Traore scoring in the first minute and looked set for a shock win until Ahmed Ben Ali equalised in the final 10 minutes.
Raja won 2-0 away against Senegal's SONACOS for a convincing 5-1 aggregate scoreline.

Another previous winner, Orlando Pirates of South Africa, struggled through a goalless draw with Roma Rovers in neighbourng Lesotho where an extra 15000 spectators crammed into the 30,000-capacity Sesotho stadium.
Two people were injured when railings collapsed under their weight at halftime. Pirates won 1-0 on aggregate to set up a mouth-watering tie with Zimbabwean neighbours Caps United.

The tie on the remote Cape Verdian island between Desportivo Travadores and Mouloudia Alger was postponed to Monday night after the scheduled match officials failed to arrived. Substitute referees from Sierra Leone flew to Praia on Monday to handle the game.
Mouloudia Alger led 6-1 from the first leg two weeks ago.

Arab Contractors scored twice in the first half-hour to beat Mumias Sugar and are joined in the second round of the Cup Winners' Cup by compatriots Mansoura, Royal Armed Forces of Morocco, Tunisia's Etoile Sahel and Mouloudia Oran of Algeria.
Etoile Sahel completed a remarkable comeback against Burkina Faso's Etoile Filante, winning 4-0 for 4-3 aggregate triumph.
CAF Cup holders Kawkab Marrakesh won 1-0 away at Senegal's ASC la Lingurere for a 2-0 aggregate win, with Yani scoring after 30 minutes.
